text:
mira: Hey team — hitting an import error after pip installing the Python SDK on my M1 Mac. wheel downloaded looks x86_64 and import fails with dyld error. Anyone seen this?

joel: Can you paste python -V and pip debug --verbose? Also the pip install output where it shows the wheel filename.

mira: python -V -> Python 3.11.4
pip --version -> pip 23.2.1 from /Users/mira/.pyenv/versions/3.11.4/envs/appenv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/pip (python 3.11)

pip install output snippet:
```
Collecting redwood-sdk
  Downloading redwood_sdk-1.4.2-cp311-cp311-macosx_10_9_x86_64.whl (2.1 MB)
Installing collected packages: redwood-sdk
Successfully installed redwood-sdk-1.4.2
```

When I import:
```
>>> import redwood_sdk
ImportError: dlopen(/Users/mira/.pyenv/versions/3.11.4/envs/appenv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood_c_ext.cpython-311-darwin.so, 2): Library not loaded: @rpath/libpython3.11.dylib
  Reason: no suitable image found.  Did find: /.../macosx_10_9_x86_64/libpython3.11.dylib: mach-o, but wrong architecture
```

sam: That wheel is clearly built for x86_64 only (see macosx_10_9_x86_64). pip picked it because there isn't an arm64 wheel available. Two quick options: 1) force building from source so it compiles for arm64, or 2) run under an x86_64 Python (Rosetta) so the x86 wheel works.

joel: To force source build try:
```
pip install --no-binary :all: redwood-sdk
```
But if the package has a compiled extension you'll need the Rust/C toolchain available. Share the build error if it fails.

mira: Tried --no-binary. Build failed with this: 
```
ERROR: redwood-c-ext v0.9.1 failed to compile
error: could not find `cargo`
```
I don't have rust installed in this env.

sam: OK then either install Rust toolchain (rustup) or use the prebuilt wheel but under the matching arch. On mac, easiest is to use a universal2 wheel from releases. I'll escalate.

mira: Is there a way to tell pip to prefer arm64 wheel if one existed?

joel: pip relies on wheel tags. If we uploaded a macosx_11_0_arm64.whl or universal2, pip would pick it on arm64 Python. You can inspect supported tags with:
```
python -c "import pip._internal.utils.compatibility_tags as t; print(list(t.get_supported()))"
```
or run `pip debug --verbose` to see interpreter tags.

mira: sharing pip debug --verbose output attached (shows cp311-cp311-macosx_10_9_x86_64 in candidates).

sam: I'll open an internal issue for the build team to publish an arm64/universal wheel. In the meantime, quick workarounds: (A) install rust toolchain and build from source: `brew install rustup-init && rustup-init` then `pip install --no-binary :all: redwood-sdk` (B) use an x86_64 Python under Rosetta: `arch -x86_64 /usr/local/bin/python3 -m pip install redwood-sdk` (C) use a linux container (CI) to run workloads server-side.

mira: I tried installing rust via brew and reran `pip install --no-binary :all:` — build succeeded and import works now. Good to know. Thanks!

ci-bot: Created issue INF-482: "macos arm64 wheel missing for redwood-sdk (universal2)" and assigned to @alex.

alex: Thanks for the report, Mira. I'll investigate the CI wheel matrix and add building universal2 wheels for macos to the release job. ETA: next patch release.

mira: Awesome — thanks all. Workaround (install rust + --no-binary) fixed it for my dev machine. Closing for now :thumbsup:
